docs:
## Purpose

Use Text Swap when a short, changing label or status benefits from a brief visual acknowledgement. Typical uses include request state, save state, selected filters, and compact call to action labels. Use ordinary text when the content is static or when the update needs a larger status region. Text Swap inherits the Consumer Theme rather than applying an Aeri UI theme.

## Installation

Install with the Aeri UI registry command shown on this Item Page. Preview installations configure the Aeri UI registry URL in `components.json`.

## API and anatomy

`TextSwap` requires string or numeric `content` and a stable `contentKey`. Change both when the meaning of the content changes. The key describes the identity of the displayed state and starts one visual transition. Set `reducedMotion` when an application preference must suppress motion in addition to the system preference. Text Swap also preserves native span props and forwards its ref. The API exposes no Catalog utility or raw motion timing control.

## Dependencies and client boundary

Text Swap has no runtime dependency beyond React. Its short native Web Animation requires a client boundary. The Catalog Live Preview adds further client state only to expose controls.

## Accessibility

Visual transition layers are hidden from assistive technology. A polite atomic status exposes the supplied final content, so the meaningful state change is announced without intermediate animation frames. Pass native `aria-live=off` when another nearby status already communicates the same change. Text Swap has no keyboard interaction of its own.

## Motion and performance

Each key change uses transform and opacity animations for incoming and outgoing content. When the width changes, one measured inline width animation prevents the surrounding layout from jumping; this limited layout animation is necessary because localized content cannot be known in advance. All animations finish after 400 milliseconds and create no timer or animation frame loop. System or explicit reduced motion skips every animation and presents the final content immediately. Browser checks cover response time, width continuity, and settled work.

## Consumer Theme

Text Swap inherits the Consumer Theme color, font, weight, and appearance. Use `className` for local typography or layout. The source does not add a global stylesheet, rewrite global tokens, or call a remote service.

## Responsive, localization, and RTL

Supply localized content directly through `content` and use a stable key for each localized state. The visual layers share one intrinsic inline grid, so short, long, and localized values remain aligned during a transition. Text direction and bidirectional text rendering follow the Consumer Project.

## Compatibility

Text Swap supports Next.js 16 App Router Consumer Projects using React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, and shadcn in evergreen browsers with the Web Animations API. It works in light and dark Consumer Theme appearances and remains functional offline after installation.
